events.event:
Mom and Miranda moved into the apartment. Mom cleaned the room.
They met Louisa and Sal by the garbage can.
events.note:
1. Miranda asked her mom to tell the story again and again. 
2. Sal stopped crying the moment he saw Miranda. 
3. The apartment was filthy, worn, and old.

events.event: Mira and Sal used to be close friends who seemed to be part of each other.
Mira and Sal saw a strange man who had shown up on their corner. (Mom told Mira not to call him Quack, so Mira called him the laughing man.)
events.note:
1. Mira and Sal were scared, but they pretended not to be.  
2. The laughing man slept under a mailbox. He chanted “Bookbag, Pocketshoe.” He hit his head with his fists. Maybe he was insane.

events.event: Mira questioned Richard about the strange things the laughing man did, but Richard couldn't explain them clearly.

Mom got the postcard for the $20,000 Pyramid.
Miranda is supposed to write a letter to tell the true story to “You", who is already gone.
events.note:
1. Her friend, “You,” could tell the future.
“You” sent Miranda some notes.
She might not write the letter because “You” are gone and there is no one to give it to.
Glossy red hair; a tiny woman.

events.event: Miranda is helping Mom prepare for the contest. (Richard will come to help, too.)
events.note:
Mom has a boyfriend named Richard.
Mom has been in a relationship with Richard for almost two years.
Richard doesn't have a key to their home. Richard thinks keys are powerful.
Richard is a handsome/tucked-in man.——Mr. Perfect

events.event:
Miranda had left her keys at school and waited for her mom at Belle's Market.
Belle and Miranda talked about a book (Meg).
Miranda and her mom discussed the origin of Miranda's name.
events.note:
Robbie B. is Miranda's schoolmate. His father is a prosecutor.
Shakespeare created the name Miranda. Mom wanted Miranda to have qualities such as humanism and compassion. The name stands for people's rights. The Miranda warnings stand for people's rights.

events.event: They hid a key in the nozzle of the fire hose.
events.note:
“You” asked me to mention the key, which I probably won't.
Inference: “You” are dead.
There is a 20% chance Miranda will write the letter. Why does Miranda still think she may write it?
If Miranda ever writes the letter, she will tell “You” where the key is.

The rules of the Speed Round.
Tenant-meeting night—once a month—the old folks and Louisa come out of loyalty to Mom.
Mom is practicing for the Speed Round.
Poor living conditions.

events.event: Mom and Richard are practicing. Mira is trying to figure out what “You” wanted.
events.note: Mira is not sure what the true story is. But she thinks the whole ture story began the day Sal got punched.
